newsitem.title: JAPAN: JAL to import Australia jet fuel.
newsitem.headline: JAL to import Australia jet fuel.

text.p: Japan Airlines Co Ltd (JAL) said on Monday it would import jet fuel from Australia to cut costs, in a move made possible the liberalisation of oil product imports in April.
It will be the first time JAL has imported jet fuel itself. It normally buys jet fuel from Japanese oil firms.
The shipment of 30,000 kilolitres (kl) of jet fuel, which costs about 700 million yen, is due to arrive at the port of Chiba near Tokyo this month, a JAL spokesman said.
He declined to reveal JAL's partner in the deal.
JAL is considering buying more spot jet fuel from a wide range of overseas oil firms, and plans to cut costs by about one billion yen a year through direct imports, he said.
Term contracts would also be a possibility if conditions were favourable, the JAL spokesman said.

Before deregulation in April, oil firms enjoyed the sole right to import oil products such as gasoline, kerosene and gas oil. Japanese airlines had to go through the oil firms to meet their domestic needs.
Theoretically, any company can now import oil products.
